title: Hardship and Protective Holds — Extension Terms, with Long-Term Hardship Hold Extensions Through the Self-Service Portal
content:
## Terms of extension

Under Hardship and Protective Holds, a running Long-Term Hardship Hold may be extended up to the tier's maximum number of extensions, each extension adding the days the long-term extension adds to the hold's end date; a running Military Service Hold is extended under its own extension rule, and a running hold of any other tier may be extended at the consumer's request up to the tier's maximum number of extensions, each extension adding the tier's extension days to its end date.

The extension is the consumer's own election: once the updated documentation the tier requires is on record and the request falls inside the tier's extension window, the consumer books it in person through the self-service portal, and the desk tells the consumer the days the long-term extension adds.

For a Long-Term Hardship Hold, as for a hold of every other tier, the hold's current end date is the end date on record: the start date plus the initial hold days minus 1, plus the days each extension already granted added, counted in calendar days with the last day included, and the hold completes its term on that date.

An extension is refused when the tier counts toward the annual limit and the hold days in the rolling 12 months plus the days the extension adds would exceed the tier's rolling 12-month maximum, the days the extension adds being, for a Long-Term Hardship Hold, the days the long-term extension adds and, for any other tier that counts toward the limit, the tier's extension days.

The consumer's own booking through the portal is the decision on a Long-Term Hardship Hold extension and takes effect the day it is made; a Military Service Hold extension is decided under its own extension rule, and an extension of a hold of any other tier is decided within the tier's extension decision days, counted as business days.

## The terms as conditions and effects

| Condition or effect | Content |
|---|---|
| Hold concerned | A running Long-Term Hardship Hold |
| How many extensions | Up to the tier's maximum number of extensions |
| Who books it | The consumer, in person, through the self-service portal |
| Before booking | The updated documentation the tier requires is on record, and the request falls inside the tier's extension window |
| The desk's part | Telling the consumer the days the long-term extension adds |
| Refusal | Where the tier counts toward the annual limit and the rolling 12-month hold days plus the days the long-term extension adds would exceed the tier's rolling 12-month maximum |
| Decision and effect | The consumer's booking is the decision and takes effect the day it is made |

## Holds of the other tiers

| Tier | Extension | Days each extension adds | Current end date | Annual-limit refusal | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Military Service Hold | Under its own extension rule | Under its own extension rule | The end date on record | — | Under its own extension rule |
| Any other tier | At the consumer's request, up to the tier's maximum number of extensions | The tier's extension days | The end date on record | Where the tier counts toward the limit, using the tier's extension days | Within the tier's extension decision days, counted as business days |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A running Documented Hardship Hold whose end date on record is 30 September is extended at the consumer's request; each extension adds the tier's extension days to that end date, and the extension is decided within the tier's extension decision days, counted as business days.

## Tool card: `extend_longterm_hold_aa9e035f`

**Capability.** The consumer extends their own running Long-Term Hardship Hold through the self-service portal. One call books one extension: it records the extension in the hold history with today's date, the extension's sequence number and the days added, and moves the hold's end date on record — its last covered day — forward by those days, counting the extension count up by one. The hold stays active. On success the consumer and the desk see the new last day of the hold and the extension in its history.

**How it is invoked.** This is the consumer's own tool. The agent unlocks `extend_longterm_hold_aa9e035f` and hands it over; the customer themselves — the consumer — runs it in person through the portal.

**Parameters.**

- `hold_id` — the hold reference number of the consumer's running hold, which the agent reads from the hardship hold lookup and gives to the consumer. Identifier format.
- `extension_days` — the days the extension adds, in calendar days, that the agent tells the consumer; a whole number of at least 1, no decimals. The new last day of the hold is the current last day plus this many days.

**Return.** A dictionary rendered as text with `extension_ref` (the reference of the recorded extension), `hold_id`, `extension_number` (which extension of the hold this is, an integer), `days_added` (calendar days, an integer), `previous_end_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `new_end_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, the hold's new last covered day) and `status`, which is always `extended` when the extension is booked.

**Input and receipt (hypothetical).** On a hold whose last covered day is 31 August, a booking with `extension_days` of 40 returns a `previous_end_date` of 31 August and a `new_end_date` of 10 October.
